examples.question_text: A population has mean $150$ and standard deviation $24$. An independent random sample of $64$ values has mean $154.5$. Find the $z$-score of this sample mean.
examples.solution_text:
The standard deviation of the sample mean is
$\begin{align*}\sigma_{\bar{X}}&=\frac{24}{\sqrt{64}}\\&=3.\end{align*}$
Standardise using this spread:
$\begin{align*}z&=\frac{154.5-150}{3}\\&=1.5.\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: A population has mean $200$ g and standard deviation $30$ g. An independent random sample of $100$ items is taken. Using the empirical rule, estimate (a) $P(\bar{X}>206)$ and (b) $P(\bar{X}>197)$.
A population has mean $80$ and standard deviation $18$. An independent random sample of $81$ values is taken. Using the empirical rule, estimate (a) $P(76<\bar{X}<84)$ and (b) $P(78<\bar{X}<84)$.

A population has mean $110$ and standard deviation $25$. An independent random sample of $100$ values is taken. Estimate (a) $P(\bar{X}>113)$ and (b) $P(\bar{X}<108)$ using the table.
$\begin{array}{c|c}z&P(Z<z)\\\hline0.80&0.7881\\1.20&0.8849\end{array}$
examples.solution_text:
The sampling distribution is approximately normal, with
$\begin{align*}\sigma_{\bar{X}}&=\frac{25}{\sqrt{100}}\\&=2.5.\end{align*}$
(a)
$\begin{align*}z&=\frac{113-110}{2.5}\\&=1.2.\\P(\bar{X}>113)&\approx P(Z>1.2)\\&=1-0.8849\\&=0.1151.\end{align*}$
(b) Use symmetry for the negative boundary:
$\begin{align*}z&=\frac{108-110}{2.5}\\&=-0.8.\\P(\bar{X}<108)&\approx P(Z<-0.8)\\&=1-P(Z<0.8)\\&=1-0.7881\\&=0.2119.\end{align*}$

examples.question_text:
Individual package masses are normally distributed with mean $400$ g and standard deviation $20$ g. Compare a single package with the mean of an independent random sample of $64$ packages. Find the $z$-score of $405$ g in each case and the probability of exceeding $405$ g, using the table.
$\begin{array}{c|c}z&P(Z<z)\\\hline0.25&0.5987\\2.00&0.9772\end{array}$
examples.solution_text:
For a single package, use the population standard deviation:
$\begin{align*}z_X&=\frac{405-400}{20}\\&=0.25.\\P(X>405)&=1-0.5987\\&=0.4013.\end{align*}$
For the sample mean, use
$\begin{align*}\sigma_{\bar{X}}&=\frac{20}{\sqrt{64}}\\&=2.5\text{ g}.\\z_{\bar{X}}&=\frac{405-400}{2.5}\\&=2.\\P(\bar{X}>405)&=1-0.9772\\&=0.0228.\end{align*}$
Both distributions are normal because the population is normal. The sample mean has the smaller spread and the larger $z$-score, so its right-tail probability is smaller.

examples.question_text: A population has mean $90$ and standard deviation $40$. Independent random samples of $100$ values are taken. Using the empirical rule, estimate (a) the boundary $c$ for which $P(\bar{X}>c)\approx0.16$, (b) the interval symmetric about $90$ containing the middle $95\%$ of sample means, and (c) the width of the interval containing the middle $68\%$.
examples.solution_text:
The sampling distribution is approximately normal, with
$\begin{align*}\sigma_{\bar{X}}&=\frac{40}{\sqrt{100}}\\&=4.\end{align*}$
(a) A right-tail area of approximately $0.16$ corresponds to $z=1$.
$\begin{align*}c&=90+1(4)\\&=94.\end{align*}$
(b) The middle $95\%$ corresponds approximately to $-2<Z<2$.
$\begin{align*}\text{Lower boundary}&=90-2(4)=82,\\\text{Upper boundary}&=90+2(4)=98.\end{align*}$
The interval is approximately $82<\bar{X}<98$.
(c) The middle $68\%$ corresponds approximately to $-1<Z<1$, giving boundaries $86$ and $94$.
$\begin{align*}\text{Width}&=94-86\\&=8.\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: A population has mean $100$ and standard deviation $27$. Find the size of an independent random sample for which the standard deviation of the sample mean is $3$. Then use the empirical rule to estimate $P(\bar{X}>106)$.
examples.solution_text:
Solve for the sample size:
$\begin{align*}\frac{27}{\sqrt{n}}&=3,\\\sqrt{n}&=9,\\n&=81.\end{align*}$
Since $n=81\ge30$, use the approximately normal sampling distribution.
$\begin{align*}z&=\frac{106-100}{3}\\&=2.\\P(\bar{X}>106)&\approx P(Z>2)\\&\approx\frac{1-0.95}{2}\\&=0.025.\end{align*}$
